Include appropriate shampoos, conditioners, and any other products.  Talk about the types of tools that are best to ensure this dog's coat remains matt and tangle-free.  It should make clear how much time one could expect to spend on this entire process.  Include a numbered list, but also include a short intro and conclusion of one or two sentences each.  The numbered list should be a list of ten steps.  One of the steps should be gathering the correct products and tools.

arguments.content:
A Maltese’s silky single coat tangles easily, so a careful, product-supported bath and blow-dry routine is the fastest way to keep it bright, light, and mat-free. Plan ahead, work gently, and keep the coat hydrated so it dries straight instead of knotting.

1) **Gather the correct products and tools (5–10 min).**  
   **Shampoos (choose one):** gentle, dog-specific, moisturizing/whitening if desired (e.g., **Chris Christensen White on White**, **iGroom Squalane + Keratin**, **Isle of Dogs Tearless Puppy**, **Earthbath Oatmeal & Aloe**).  
   **Conditioner (highly recommended):** a rich rinse-out conditioner (e.g., **Chris Christensen Ice on Ice Conditioner**, **iGroom Argan + Vitamin E Conditioner**, **Isle of Dogs Silky Coating Conditioner**).  
   **Detangler/leave-in (for drying):** light spray to prevent tangles (e.g., **Chris Christensen Ice on Ice Finishing Spray**, **The Stuff**).  
   **Optional products:** tear stain facial cleanser (dog-safe), whitening paste for paws/muzzle, dog-safe ear cleaner, cotton balls for ears (not inside canal).  
   **Tools:** slicker brush (soft pins), long-pin pin brush, stainless steel greyhound comb (fine/medium), dematting tool or mat splitter (for small tight mats only), microfiber towel + absorbent bath towel, high-velocity dryer (variable speed) and/or stand dryer, grooming table/non-slip mat, spray bottle for diluting products, nail trimmers if doing nails after.

2) **Pre-brush and pre-detangle on a dry coat (10–20 min).**  
   Before water touches the coat, gently remove tangles—water tightens knots into mats. Mist lightly with a detangling spray, then **line-brush** (part the coat in layers, brush from skin outward). Follow with a greyhound comb; if the comb can’t pass through, keep working the area gently. If you find tight mats, use fingers first; only use a dematting tool sparingly to avoid coat breakage and skin irritation.

3) **Prep the bath area and protect ears/eyes (2–5 min).**  
   Place a non-slip mat in the tub/sink. Use lukewarm water (not hot). You can place a cotton ball at the opening of each ear to reduce water entry (remove after the bath). Apply a small amount of mineral oil or dog-safe eye lubricant around eyes only if recommended by your groomer/vet; otherwise simply avoid splashing the face.

4) **Thoroughly wet the coat (3–8 min).**  
   Saturate the coat all the way to the skin. A Maltese coat repels water at first; take your time. Proper wetting helps shampoo spread evenly and reduces friction (which causes tangles).

5) **First shampoo: cleanse (5–10 min).**  
   Dilute shampoo (commonly **1:5 to 1:10**, follow label) in a bottle/cup to reduce tangling and ensure even coverage. Massage gently with fingertips (avoid scrubbing in circles). Focus on legs, underside, and areas that collect dirt. Rinse extremely well—leftover shampoo makes the coat dull and itchy and increases matting.

6) **Second shampoo (optional but common): brighten/condition the coat (5–10 min).**  
   If your Maltese needs extra brightening or is oily, do a second wash with the same shampoo or a whitening shampoo. Keep contact time per label directions. Rinse until water runs clear and the coat feels “squeaky clean” without residue.

7) **Conditioner: rehydrate and detangle (5–10 min + rinse).**  
   Apply a rinse-out conditioner from mid-lengths to ends, then lightly to the roots (avoid heavy buildup at the skin). Use your fingers to distribute; you can gently comb through with a wide end of the greyhound comb while conditioner is in (very carefully). Let sit **2–5 minutes**. Rinse well, but don’t strip it completely—aim for a soft, slippery feel that helps prevent knots.

8) **Towel-dry correctly (5–10 min).**  
   Press and squeeze with a microfiber towel—**do not rub** (rubbing creates tangles and frizz). You can wrap the body in a towel “robe” for a minute to absorb water, then replace with a dry towel. If the coat is long, keep it lying straight as you blot.

9) **Apply leave-in + blow dry while brushing (20–45 min).**  
   Mist a leave-in detangler/finishing spray lightly over the coat (avoid eyes). Using a dryer on warm/low heat, start at the body and work systematically in sections. For mat prevention, use **line-drying**: lift a thin layer of coat, blow air at the roots until dry, then move down the hair shaft. Brush with a slicker or pin brush as you dry, always supporting the coat to avoid pulling. A high-velocity dryer speeds drying but can tangle if used too close or too strong—keep it moving and reduce speed for fine coats.

10) **Final comb-out and finishing check (5–15 min).**  
   When the coat is fully dry (dampness creates knots later), comb from skin to ends with the greyhound comb. Check friction areas: behind ears, armpits, inner thighs, collar/harness line, and around the tail. Touch up with a tiny amount of leave-in spray if you find snags. Reward your dog and note any recurring mat spots so you can brush those areas more often between baths.

**Time expectation:** For most Maltese coats, expect **~60–120 minutes total** (shorter coat/experienced handler on the low end; long coat/more tangles on the high end). The blow-dry-and-brush step is usually the longest and most important for preventing mats.

With the right moisture-focused products, gentle section-by-section brushing, and a complete dry-and-comb finish, a Maltese coat stays light, straight, and far less prone to tangles. Consistency matters—regular brushing between baths makes each full grooming session faster and more comfortable.
